span: observed that title can be based on adverse possession
why: The court reports an earlier decision saying title can be based on adverse possession and that the law is harsh; the current court's adoption is not shown in this passage, so no court stance is recorded.

span: a co-owner, can under law, claim title by adverse possession against another co-owner
why: Quoted earlier decision on ouster by a co-owner; it is a narrower point (co-owners) and adoption by the current court is not shown here.

span: A person who sets up a plea of adverse possession must establish both possession which is peaceful, open and continuous possession
why: Quotes M. Siddiq on the requirements of the plea; the court's own conclusion that the defendants fail is in the next paragraph.

span: The respondent failed to discharge the onus.
why: Court states the requirements for adverse possession and rejects the claim on facts; it does not deny that title can be acquired, so the stance is MIXED.

span: can acquire title through adverse possession even if it is the property of the waqf
why: Headnote holding that a waqf beneficiary can acquire title by adverse possession, supporting acquisition against the owner; headnote confidence is capped.

span: the possessory owner acquires an absolute title
why: Headnote holding stating that an owner who does not assert his right within the limitation period loses it and the possessor acquires an absolute title, applied to the defendant.

span: he could claim to have perfected his title by adverse possession
why: Quotes an earlier decision that an alternative plea of title and adverse possession is available; the current court's adoption is not shown in the passage.
